recentItems.title: Prisoners react after early release #EarlyRelease #England #Wales #Prisons
recentItems.description:
We spoke with prisoners released early from HMP Berwyn in Wales, as the government's early release scheme has taken effect across England and Wales.

Hundreds of prisoners are being released early to try and ease overcrowding in prisons.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Some prisoners said conditions in HMP Berwyn were poor, and others express some concern about the effect releasing inmates early could have on the country.

Critics and victims say the probation service is not equipped to handle the influx of released prisoners and are worried about the prospect of reoffending.

recentItems.title: Death row inmate survives execution attempt
recentItems.description:
A death row inmate in the United States has survived two attempts to execute her by lethal injection.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Christa Pike’s execution, in the state of Tennessee, was halted and she was taken to hospital when she was still alive after two injections.

Now 50-years-old, Pike was sentenced to death in 1996 aged 18 for murdering her 19-year-old schoolmate Colleen Slemmer.

The Tennessee Department of Correction said it followed every step of the state’s lawful, established execution protocol.

Lawyers and human rights experts had heavily opposed Christa’s execution, given her age at the time of sentencing. Just an hour before her scheduled death, the US Supreme Court ruled that the execution was allowed to take place.

Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has now halted the one remaining execution for the rest of the year.

Warning: this video contains content some viewers may find distressing.

recentItems.title: Why ‘oil shocks’ will hit bank accounts across UK
recentItems.description:
How does the price of oil impact your bank balance?

Household budgets are being squeezed right now over fuel, shopping and energy bills. Fuel prices in the UK have hit record highs.

Energy bills are forecast to see the biggest surge in four years in January, and the Bank of England has warned that interest rates could increase in November - again.

It’s another example of how foreign conflict - like Yemen, Iran and in Ukraine - is pushing up prices in the UK.

So, in this episode of the breakdown, we speak to Dr Sugandha Srivastav, Lecturer in Environmental Economics at the University of Oxford, to look at the chain reaction being caused by conflict thousands of miles away.

We explore why prices shoot up so quickly, but seem to take much longer to come down, and whether there is anything the UK can actually do to protect itself from the next ‘oil shock’.

-------

Presenter: Anja Popp
Producer: Suzannah Rogerson

recentItems.title: Andy Burnham floats idea of UK rejoining EU
recentItems.description:
The UK could go 'all the way back' into the EU, says Prime Minister Andy Burnham who is looking at a range of options from doing nothing to rejoining. 

Burnham has raised the possibility of Britain rejoining the European Union, as the Labour Party conference came to an end in Liverpool.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

In an interview with Channel 4 News, he said Britain was “drifting” and the decade since Brexit hadn’t been good enough.   

He said the country needed an “honest conversation”  about its relationship with Europe, with no options ruled out. 

The Brexit debate is well and truly back, where will it lead us?

Reporter: Gary Gibbon
Producer: Robert Hamilton, Meghan Hadfield, Kirsty O'Driscoll

recentItems.title: Flydubai latest: Pilot arrested after co-pilot stabbed on flight bound for Israel
recentItems.description:
A flydubai flight bound for Israel descended into chaos as a pilot appeared to stab another and its claimed he intended to crash the plane.

One of the Israeli passengers who helped to foil a potential terror attack on board the plane headed to Tel Aviv has described how he and another man forced their way into the cockpit as one of the pilots was trying to destroy the controls, before putting him in a choke hold and pulling him away. 

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Other off-duty pilots who were travelling on the flight managed to land the flydubai plane safely in Saudi Arabia where the pilot who launched the alleged attack was arrested. 

Israeli politicians claim it was an act of terrorism but no authorities have yet said what actually happened.

A warning, there are distressing images in this report.

recentItems.title: What next for Man City after their £900m ‘SHAM’?
recentItems.description:
In a seismic ruling that has sent shockwaves through football, Manchester City have been found guilty of dozens of financial charges spanning a nine-year period from 2009 to 2018. The club were found to have systematically misstated financial accounts, arranged disguised funding through "sham" sponsorship agreements, and failed to cooperate in good faith with the league's four-year investigation.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

While Manchester City have denied the findings and said they plan to appeal the findings, what punishment could they face - a points deduction? Relegation?

In this episode of The Fourcast, Jordan Jarrett-Bryan is joined by chief football writer Darren Lewis and football finance expert Kieran Maguire, the panel interrogates how badly the Premier League’s brand has been tarnished, what punishments the club could face, and whether the integrity of the modern game can survive.
